title: US defaults on debt by 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States federal government fails to make a scheduled payment on any Treasury note, bond, or bill at any point between November 5, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, or Fitch publicly classify any U.S. sovereign debt as being in default during the qualifying period this will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Standard & Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch.

eventMetadata.context_description: The recent increase of the statutory debt limit to $41.1 trillion through the 2025 reconciliation legislation has created substantial headroom, with projections showing the ceiling likely binding only in late 2027 at the earliest. Congress has repeatedly raised or suspended the limit over decades to avoid any interruption in Treasury payments, reflecting strong institutional incentives against default on obligations. This track record, combined with the Treasury’s use of extraordinary measures as a backstop, underpins the 97.4% trader consensus against default by 2027. Even so, an unprecedented congressional impasse extending beyond available cash reserves and accounting maneuvers could still shift outcomes in that window.
